summary: Inventory application is available on node1 at TCP port 8181. SELinux remains enforcing, firewalld permits the port, and the service persisted across a verified node restart. The RHEL release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Configured Apache to listen on TCP 8181 and enabled it at boot.
Deployed the inventory application page with the httpd_sys_content_t SELinux label.
Assigned TCP 8181 to SELinux type http_port_t.
Added TCP 8181 to runtime and permanent firewalld configuration.
Restarted node1 and verified complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Serve the inventory application over TCP 8181
evidence.summary: Apache configuration uses port 8181; the listener is active; direct requests to node1 return HTTP 200 and the Inventory Application content.
SELinux is Enforcing, TCP 8181 is labeled http_port_t, application content is correctly labeled, and Apache processes run in httpd_t.

evidence.requirement: Permit access through the host firewall
evidence.summary: TCP 8181 is allowed in both runtime and permanent firewalld configuration, including after restart.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 remained unchanged; Apache 2.4.62 is the Red Hat-provided RHEL 9 package.

Healthy baseline boot ID c2f29441-0515-4717-99f7-a7647824278d was captured, restart was acknowledged, the new boot ID c48410df-cf19-49e5-acba-dcf346650f78 proved a node restart, and post-restart checks confirmed the enabled/active service, listener, HTTP 200 application data, SELinux enforcement, firewall persistence, release, and kernel.
